title: Multi-year drift and calibration interval for the SHT40-class MiniNode accuracy claim
question: What do peer-reviewed field-stability, accelerated-aging and intercomparison studies establish about the long-term drift, hysteresis and contamination sensitivity of SHT40-class capacitive RH/T sensors in cold, humid enclosures over one to five years, and what calibration interval or field check is required before a MiniNode can state a product accuracy over a multi-year no-cloud deployment rather than only a 72-hour bench comparison?
why_now: The MiniNode environment handoff makes 'stable sensor response' a P2 acceptance condition, while the planned Gen-0 validation is only a 72-hour run against a reference. Because the product promise is local-first operation over a multi-year battery life, an accuracy statement without a drift and calibration basis cannot outlive the bench test.
real_world_anchor: Measured long-term drift and field stability of low-cost capacitive RH/T sensors (SHT40/SHT3x class), accelerated-aging behaviour, and calibration-transfer practice in environmental metrology.
novelty_reason: The prior MiniNode metrology topic bounds the 72-hour enclosure response, condensation bias and reference traceability for a bench run. It does not address drift, hysteresis or calibration interval across the multi-year life implied by the >2-year battery and no-cloud product promise; this gap adds the product-lifetime accuracy and maintenance dimension and asks whether a one-time calibration can sustain a stated accuracy.
